articles.title: Teen girl who livestreamed San Diego mosque shooting faces murder charges, prosecutors say
articles.summary: A 17-year-old girl accused of livestreaming a deadly attack on a San Diego mosque is now facing murder charges.
articles.body:
A 17-year-old girl accused of livestreaming a deadly attack on a San Diego mosque is now facing murder charges.

The North Carolina teen was indicted Monday on three counts of murder and one count of conspiracy in the San Diego mosque shooting that killed three men, authorities said.

The girl, identified only as a high school student in Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Schools, is accused of livestreaming the attack in which two shooters — Caleb Vazquez , 18, and Cain Clark, 17 — opened fire at the Islamic Center of San Diego on May 18, Forsyth County Dist. Atty. Jim O'Neill announced at a news conference Monday. She is also accused of publishing the shooters' manifesto in an effort to spread their credo of hate, and of failing to report the planned mosque attack to law enforcement.

The girl also knew that the shooters had intended to follow up their initial rampage by committing mass murders at a local Jewish temple and a predominantly Black high school the same day, O'Neill said. The additional shootings did not take place, as Vazquez and Clark took their own lives inside a car a few blocks away from the mosque.

Though the girl was not physically present in California, O'Neill said that there is enough evidence to charge her with murder for aiding and abetting the attack as she shared the shooters' criminal intent and was in a position to render aid during the crime. The girl was arrested last week and indicted by a grand jury Monday.

"The law in North Carolina is clear: A person may be guilty of a crime, although he or she personally does not do any of the acts necessary to constitute the crime," he said. At 17 years old, she can be tried as an adult for her charges in North Carolina, he added.

Authorities were aware early on that three people watched a livestream of the attack, which was captured via GoPro cameras on helmets worn by the two shooters, he said. However, it took months to gather the evidence necessary to identify and prosecute the person allegedly responsible for disseminating it.

A coalition of local and federal law enforcement agencies conducted more than 100 interviews and 30 search warrants and reviewed more than 4 million messages as part of the investigation, according to Reid Davis, special agent in charge of the FBI's Charlotte Field Office.

Authorities believe that the girl was radicalized in the same extremist online networks as Vazquez and Clark and communicated with them using the messaging platform Signal, O'Neill said.

"[In] this underground subculture of hate, they listen to each other, they talk to each other in encoded platforms," O'Neill said. "It radicalizes one another to the point where they carry out these horrific crimes of violence and murder."

O'Neill said that the goal of publishing the livestream was to "memorialize the two terrorists," and that it is important that the charges send a strong message that "what happened back in May of 2026 should not be something anybody should be watching or glorifying."

He also urged parents to pay close attention to their children's online activity, noting the ease with which teenagers can enter dark corners of the internet.

"You have to know what your kids are doing, who they're talking to, what they're getting into," he said.

Davis said he hoped that Monday's charges would serve as a reminder that anyone who becomes aware of plans for violence should report them immediately to law enforcement. He said he hoped the indictment would bring some sense of comfort to the victims in San Diego.

"To the families who lost loved ones, to the families who are at worship, and to the entire San Diego community," he said, "you remain in our prayers."

The three men killed in the attack were Amin Abdullah, Mansour Kaziha and Nadir Awad. Abdullah, a longtime security guard, was praised for his heroic actions confronting the shooters and giving others time to flee.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Moradores relatam medo durante temporal com ventos de 110 km/h em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Manhã foi de limpeza de estragos e contabilização de prejuízos após a tempestade que atingiu Varginha na noite de segunda-feira (31). Ninguém se feriu.
articles.summary: Em Varginha, a manhã foi de limpeza de estragos e contabilização de prejuízos após a tempestade que atingiu a cidade na noite de segunda-feira (31). Ninguém se feriu.
articles.body:
A manhã desta terça-feira (1º) foi de limpeza e tentativa de recuperar os prejuízos para moradores e comerciantes de Varginha (MG), depois do temporal que atingiu a cidade na noite anterior. Árvores e galhos ficaram espalhados pelas ruas, imóveis foram destelhados e estruturas foram danificadas pela força dos ventos.

No Parque Rinaldi, uma grande telha que se desprendeu de uma padaria durante o temporal foi parar a cerca de 20 metros do estabelecimento. A estrutura caiu sobre árvores e ficou no meio da Rua Dimas Fonseca Júnior, impedindo que moradores de duas casas retirassem os carros das garagens. Galhos também ficaram espalhados pela via.

Cobertura no bairro Parque Rinaldi derrubada com a força da chuva e ventania em Varginha (MG) — Foto: Eduardo Marins/EPTV

O aposentado Deuzenir Corsetti, que mora em uma das casas atingidas pelos galhos, contou que viveu momentos de medo durante os minutos mais intensos do temporal. Segundo ele, o vento estava tão forte que precisou procurar um ponto mais protegido dentro de casa.

“Foi sensação de morte, foi o que eu senti, porque eu fiquei dentro de casa, não podia sair, porque o vento estava muito intenso.”

Deuzenir Corsetti, aposentado, conta que sentiu medo durante o temporal e precisou se proteger dentro de casa enquanto os ventos fortes atingiam o bairro Parque Rinaldi, em Varginha (MG) — Foto: Wagner Silva/EPTV

Deuzenir contou que se protegeu próximo a uma estrutura mais resistente, embaixo de uma viga e perto do fogão a lenha. Ele também relatou ter visto folhas, ciscos e outros objetos sendo levados pelo vento e ouviu o impacto da telha que atingiu a rua.

O morador disse que nunca havia presenciado uma situação semelhante desde que vive no local. “Primeira vez que acontece”, afirmou.

Segundo dados da estação meteorológica do Inmet, as rajadas de vento chegaram a 109,08 km/h em Varginha durante o temporal.

Torre de celular ficou pendurada em prédio no Centro de Varginha (MG) após temporal acompanhado de ventania — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

No Centro de Varginha, uma antena de telefonia instalada no Edifício Porto Seguro ficou parcialmente desprendida e suspensa na lateral da construção.

A aposentada Isolina Pelini de Crusatis, que mora no sexto andar, contou que ouviu um barulho muito forte durante a tempestade e chegou a pensar que o prédio poderia desabar.

Ela contou que estava na área de serviço quando começou a faltar energia. Com o prédio no escuro, um morador precisou usar uma lanterna para ajudar na circulação.

“Ouvi, e foi muito forte. Pensei que ia desabar o prédio.”

Isolina Pelini de Crusatis, aposentada, conta que levou um susto ao ouvir o forte barulho da antena se desprendendo do prédio onde mora, no Centro de Varginha (MG) — Foto: Andressa Souza/EPTV

Apesar do susto, Isolina disse que não chegou a entrar em pânico. Na manhã desta terça-feira, ela acompanhava a situação da antena à distância, já que a garagem do prédio fica em uma das áreas afetadas pela interdição.

Segundo técnicos de telefonia, a estrutura pesa aproximadamente uma tonelada. O Corpo de Bombeiros esteve no local e constatou que ela estava parcialmente desprendida, com risco de queda sobre a área externa.

Chuva e ventania derrubaram árvores, estruturas e telhas em Varginha (MG) — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Por segurança, a via pública foi isolada, e o síndico foi orientado a manter fechados os acessos ao prédio e à garagem. A antena não foi retirada porque, segundo os bombeiros, seriam necessários equipamentos e recursos técnicos que não estavam disponíveis para a equipe no momento da ocorrência.

A empresa responsável informou que a antena sofreu avarias durante o temporal e teve o funcionamento comprometido. Segundo a empresa, as manutenções preventivas e as medidas de segurança estavam em dia. Uma equipe de engenharia foi acionada para avaliar os danos e adotar as providências necessárias. O local permanece isolado por segurança.

No bairro São Geraldo, a força dos ventos arrancou o telhado da casa da aposentada Cristina Brito. A estrutura atingiu fios de alta tensão e, por orientação do Corpo de Bombeiros, ela precisou permanecer dentro da residência por horas.

Cristina contou que estava em casa quando ouviu um barulho forte e só depois percebeu que o telhado havia sido levado pelo vento.

“Eu estava aqui dentro e, de repente, aquele barulhão danado. A gente assusta na hora. Mas aí, depois que eu olhei, eu vi que o telhado estava na rua.”

Cristina Brito, aposentada, conta que teve o telhado da casa arrancado pela força dos ventos e precisou permanecer dentro da residência por orientação dos bombeiros em Varginha (MG) — Foto: Manoel Neto/EPTV

O vizinho Rubens Lorenzoni, operador de utilidade, estava assistindo televisão quando o temporal começou. Ele também se assustou com a intensidade da ventania.

“Rapaz, foi violento, viu? Acho que teve uma tempestade de quase 100 km por hora, essa ventania que teve aí.”

Rubens Lorenzoni, operador de utilidade, relata o susto com a intensidade dos ventos durante o temporal que atingiu Varginha (MG) — Foto: Manoel Neto/EPTV

O temporal provocou estragos em diversos pontos de Varginha. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, foram registrados mais de 30 atendimentos relacionados à chuva e aos ventos. Não houve registro de feridos.

A Cemig informou que mais de 90% dos imóveis afetados pela falta de energia já tiveram o fornecimento restabelecido durante a noite de segunda-feira e a madrugada desta terça.

A empresa continua trabalhando para normalizar o serviço, mas ainda não há previsão para o restabelecimento total devido à queda de árvores e ao grande número de galhos e objetos lançados sobre a rede elétrica.

articles.title: Vagas de estágio CIEE: Mais de 290 oportunidades no Vale e região | G1
articles.standfirst: Há oportunidades em diversas áreas, como setor administrativo, educação, direito, construção civil, contabilidade, marketing, informática, entre outros ramos.
articles.summary: Vagas de estágio CIEE contemplam áreas como administração, direito e TI em cidades como São José dos Campos e Jacareí, com inscrições abertas pelo portal oficial da instituição.
articles.body:
CIEE tem mais de 290 vagas de estágio abertas no Vale e região; saiba como se candidatar — Foto: Bruna Bonfim/g1

O Centro de Integração Empresa-Escola (Ciee) está com 294 vagas abertas para estágio nas cidades do Vale do Paraíba e região. Os dados foram atualizados pela instituição na última segunda-feira (31).

Os interessados devem fazer o cadastro no site e acompanhar as vagas disponíveis. Há oportunidades em diversas áreas, como setor administrativo, educação, direito, construção civil, contabilidade, marketing, informática, entre outros ramos.

Não há limite de idade para as vagas de estágio, porém, o interessado deve ter no mínimo 16 anos e estar matriculado em uma instituição de ensino para participar do processo seletivo.

Para as vagas de jovem aprendiz, os estudantes devem ter entre 14 e 24 anos incompletos e precisam estar cursando o ensino médio ou já ter concluído os estudos. A remuneração é por hora trabalhada, em regime CLT.

Os valores de bolsa-auxílio, vale-refeição e outros benefícios variam conforme a vaga e a carga horária escolhida.

Veja o número de vagas por cidade da região:

Para participar dos processos seletivos, é necessário realizar o cadastro no Portal CIEE. Na plataforma, o usuário ainda contará com cursos e poderá enriquecer o perfil para o processo seletivo por meio de vídeo-apresentação e redação online. Todas as ferramentas são disponibilizadas gratuitamente.

Os interessados podem tirar dúvidas por meio do WhatsApp no número (11) 3003-2433 do Ciee.

articles.title: Maus-tratos a animais em ONG no Rio: cães são resgatados | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Câmara Municipal, moradores chegaram a registrar uma ocorrência na delegacia antes da ação de resgate. Um vizinho disse que denuncia os maus-tratos desde 2023.
articles.summary: Maus-tratos a animais em ONG no Rio motivam resgate de cães em situação insalubre e descoberta de carcaças em decomposição no Projeto Casa da Mila.
articles.body:
Cinco carcaças de animais em avançado estado de decomposição e cães desnutridos, com doenças de pele e pelos embaraçados foram encontrados em uma casa onde funcionava uma ONG, em Oswaldo Cruz, na Zona Norte do Rio.

O local foi alvo de uma ação de resgate após denúncias de moradores da região.

Cães são resgatados em situação de maus-tratos em ONG na Zona Norte do Rio — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo a Comissão de Defesa dos Animais da Câmara Municipal, os animais estavam em condições consideradas graves de maus-tratos. A responsável pelo projeto, Camila Salata Medeiros, conhecida como Mila, não foi localizada durante a ação e, até a última atualização, não havia sido presa.

Ela é responsável pela ONG Projeto Casa da Mila. O g1 tenta contato com Camila.

A denúncia chegou ao vereador Luiz Ramos Filho, que participou do resgate. Segundo ele, moradores já haviam procurado a polícia e registrado uma ocorrência por causa das condições em que os animais eram mantidos.

"Eu faço muitos resgates, mas este de hoje foi particularmente revoltante. Os animais estavam famintos e comiam a carcaça de um cão. Todos muito sujos, com os pelos embaraçados por falta de tosa, com dermatites. Um ambiente extremamente insalubre", afirmou o vereador.

Ainda de acordo com Luiz Ramos Filho, havia suspeitas de que a responsável pelo projeto arrecadava dinheiro por meio de doações via Pix divulgadas nas redes sociais.

O vereador acionou a Secretaria Municipal de Proteção e Defesa dos Animais, que participou da ação.

"Uma parte destes animais vai para os abrigos da prefeitura e outros vão para lares temporários. Eles vão receber os cuidados médicos, serão castrados e vacinados e, depois da quarentena, serão colocados para adoção", explicou a secretária municipal de Proteção e Defesa dos Animais, Jenifer Coelho Ramos.

Segundo a Câmara Municipal, moradores chegaram a registrar uma ocorrência na delegacia antes da ação de resgate. Um vizinho disse que denuncia os maus-tratos desde 2023.

O caso é investigado pela 33ª DP (Realengo).

articles.title: Chuva forte derruba árvores e interdita ruas na região de Jundiaí | G1
articles.standfirst: Tempestades que começaram na segunda-feira (31) causaram estragos em Campo Limpo Paulista e Várzea Paulista (SP).
articles.summary: A chuva forte que atingiu o interior de São Paulo desde segunda-feira (31) causou estragos em Campo Limpo Paulista e Várzea Paulista (SP).
articles.body:
Chuva causa queda de árvores em Várzea Paulista (SP) — Foto: Prefeitura de Várzea Paulista

A chuva forte que atingiu o interior de São Paulo causou estragos em Campo Limpo Paulista e Várzea Paulista (SP) desde segunda-feira (31). As ocorrências incluem quedas de árvores, interdições de ruas e danos na infraestrutura das cidades.

A Defesa Civil esclarece que, em ocorrências envolvendo árvores ou galhos em contato com a rede elétrica, a prioridade é garantir a segurança da população e evitar intervenções que possam oferecer risco de choque elétrico.

Nesses casos, a orientação é acionar a Companhia Paulista de Força e Luz (CPFL), responsável pela rede de energia e pelos procedimentos de remoção de materiais que estejam sobre ou próximos à fiação.

Chuva causa estragos em Campo Limpo Paulista (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

Conforme apurado pela TV TEM , foram registrados 51 milímetros de chuva nas últimas 24 horas em Campo Limpo Paulista. O município está entre as 14 cidades onde mais choveu no estado de São Paulo.

Três árvores caíram e uma delas comprometeu a estrutura de um poste particular. Na tarde de segunda, uma rede de drenagem se rompeu e provocou um buraco no asfalto da Rua Ágata, no Jardim Marchetti.

Equipes do Departamento de Trânsito e da Secretaria de Obras e Serviços Públicos (SOSP) estiveram no local para realizar as manutenções necessárias.

Chuva causa estragos em Várzea Paulista (SP) — Foto: Prefeitura de Várzea Paulista

Em Várzea Paulista, na Estrada do Grilo, no bairro Mursa, uma árvore caiu sobre a fiação elétrica. O Corpo de Bombeiros esteve no local para retirar os galhos e troncos. A Defesa Civil também registrou outras quatro quedas de árvores.

Na Estrada da Gauchinha, outra árvore caiu e bloqueou a via. A remoção foi realizada com o apoio da Unidade Gestora de Meio Ambiente, e o trecho já foi liberado.

A chuva também pode ter contribuído para um acidente ocorrido na manhã desta terça-feira (1°), na Marginal do Rio Jundiaí.

Conforme exibido pela TV TEM , um motorista de 40 anos perdeu o controle da direção do carro e caiu em um córrego. Ele estava com a filha, de seis anos.

Os dois tiveram ferimentos leves. O Corpo de Bombeiros e a Polícia Militar estiveram no local para prestar socorro.

articles.title: John Ternus assume oficialmente como CEO da Apple; conheça o executivo | G1
articles.standfirst: Ternus está na Apple desde 2001 e liderou o desenvolvimento de produtos como iPhone, Mac, iPad e AirPods; Tim Cook deixa o cargo após 15 anos à frente da empresa.
articles.summary: Ternus está na Apple desde 2001 e liderou o desenvolvimento de produtos como iPhone, Mac, iPad e AirPods; Tim Cook deixa o cargo após 15 anos à frente da empresa.
articles.body:
John Ternus, de 50 anos, assumiu oficialmente a liderança da Apple nesta terça-feira (1º). O nome dele já aparece na página de executivos da empresa. (Veja na imagem abaixo).

Depois de 15 anos à frente da Apple, Tim Cook deixou o cargo de CEO na segunda-feira (31), mas continua no conselho de administração da empresa.

Em mensagem enviada aos funcionários obtida pela Bloomberg, Cook agradeceu à equipe pelos anos de trabalho. "Hoje é meu último dia como CEO da Apple. É um momento que sempre soube que chegaria um dia, e ainda assim é difícil acreditar que chegou", escreveu.

John Ternus assume oficialmente como CEO da Apple; conheça o novo comandante da empresa — Foto: Reprodução/Apple

Ternus ingressou na Apple em 2001, na equipe de design de produtos. Em 2013, tornou-se vice-presidente de Engenharia de Hardware e, em 2021, passou a integrar o time executivo como vice-presidente sênior da área.

Ao longo de sua trajetória na empresa, liderou o desenvolvimento de hardware em diversas categorias e teve papel central no lançamento de novas linhas de produtos , como iPad e AirPods, além de sucessivas gerações de iPhone, Mac e Apple Watc

Segundo a companhia, seu trabalho com a linha Mac contribuiu para tornar a categoria mais poderosa e popular globalmente em seus 40 anos de história. Entre os projetos recentes, está o lançamento do MacBook Neo, voltado a ampliar o acesso à experiência Mac.

Mais recentemente, sua equipe liderou a reformulação da linha iPhone , com destaque para os modelos iPhone 17 Pro e Pro Max, o iPhone Air, de design mais fino e resistente, e o iPhone 17.

John Ternus será novo CEO da Apple — Foto: Divulgação/Apple

Sob sua liderança, a empresa também avançou nos AirPods, com melhorias em cancelamento de ruído e recursos voltados à saúde auditiva, informou a Apple.

Ternus também liderou iniciativas voltadas à durabilidade e confiabilidade dos produtos , além de avanços em materiais e design de hardware que reduziram a pegada de carbono.

Entre as medidas estão o uso de alumínio reciclado em diferentes linhas, titânio impresso em 3D no Apple Watch Ultra 3 e melhorias na reparabilidade dos dispositivos.

Antes de ingressar na Apple, trabalhou como engenheiro mecânico na Virtual Research Systems. Ternus é formado em Engenharia Mecânica pela Universidade da Pensilvânia.

Em comunicado em abril deste ano, a empresa informou que a mudança foi aprovada por unanimidade pelo conselho de administração e faz parte de um processo de planejamento de sucessão conduzido ao longo de vários anos.

“Amo a Apple com todo o meu ser e sou profundamente grato por ter tido a oportunidade de trabalhar com uma equipe tão engenhosa, inovadora, criativa e profundamente dedicada, que tem demonstrado um compromisso inabalável em enriquecer a vida de nossos clientes e criar os melhores produtos e serviços do mundo”, disse Cook.

O executivo entrou para a Apple em 1998 e assumiu como CEO em 2011, quando Steve Jobs deixou a função . Com cerca de 15 anos no comando da companhia, Cook acabou permanecendo mais tempo no cargo do que o próprio Jobs.

À frente da empresa, Cook supervisionou o lançamento de diversos produtos e serviços.

Entre eles estão novas categorias, como Apple Watch, AirPods e Apple Vision Pro, além de plataformas como iCloud, Apple Pay, Apple TV e Apple Music.

Durante sua gestão, o valor de mercado da Apple saltou de cerca de US$ 350 bilhões para US$ 4 trilhões — um aumento superior a 1.000%.

A receita anual quase quadruplicou no período, passando de US$ 108 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2011 para mais de US$ 416 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2025.

CEO da Apple, Tim Cook, mostra novo iPhone 16 — Foto: JUSTIN SULLIVAN / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP

Neste ano, a Apple completou 50 anos em um momento em que a indústria de tecnologia passa por uma nova onda de transformações impulsionadas pela inteligência artificial (IA) .

O avanço dessa tecnologia coloca pressão sobre a empresa para demonstrar que ainda é capaz de lançar produtos ou serviços com potencial de provocar mudanças culturais semelhantes às que marcou ao longo de sua história.

A companhia foi fundada em 1º de abril de 1976, na garagem de Steve Jobs, em Cupertino, na Califórnia.

Ao lado de Steve Wozniak, Jobs ajudou a popularizar o uso de computadores pessoais e iniciou uma trajetória que transformaria a Apple em uma das empresas mais valiosas do mundo, hoje avaliada em mais de US$ 3,6 trilhões.

Ao longo das décadas, a empresa lançou produtos que redefiniram a forma como as pessoas usam tecnologia no dia a dia.

🖥️ O Macintosh , apresentado em 1984, ajudou a tornar os computadores mais acessíveis ao público ao introduzir uma interface baseada em ícones e o uso do mouse.

📱Anos depois, o iPhone mudaria novamente o mercado ao consolidar o smartphone como centro da vida digital.

Desde seu lançamento, em 2007, mais de 3,1 bilhões de iPhones foram vendidos, gerando cerca de US$ 2,3 trilhões em receita, segundo dados da Counterpoint Research.

Outros produtos, como o Mac, o iPad e o Apple Watch, também ajudaram a consolidar uma base fiel de usuários ao redor do mundo.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Carro passa direto por passarela e cai em córrego no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente ocorreu na Baixada da Sobral, em Rio Branco, e o motorista não se feriu. Moradores reclamam da falta de sinalização e iluminação no local.
articles.summary: Acidente ocorreu na Baixada da Sobral, em Rio Branco, e o motorista não teve ferimentos. Moradores reclamam da falta de sinalização e iluminação no local.
articles.body:
Um carro caiu dentro de um córrego na noite do último domingo (30) na Travessa Tarauacá, bairro Bahia Velha, na Baixada da Sobral, em Rio Branco . O acidente ocorreu por volta das 21h30 e foi registrado por câmeras de segurança da rua.

O motorista do carro não se feriu. A reportagem, contudo, não conseguiu contato com aquele.

As imagens mostram o momento em que o acidente ocorreu. No vídeo, é possível ver dois homens conversando encostados em um carro e uma motocicleta, quando o motorista de outro veículo passa em linha reta e, ao chegar próximo da passarela do córrego, o veículo caiu dentro. ( Veja o vídeo acima )

O g1 entrou em contato com a Prefeitura de Rio Branco para pedir um posicionamento sobre a questão da sinalização da área e foi informada que iriam verificar para dar um retorno.

Felipe Feitosa de Lima, de 29 anos, morador da região, contou ao g1 nesta terça-feira (1º) que um guincho foi chamado e retirou o veículo de dentro do córrego. O motorista sofreu apenas danos materiais.

Carro caiu dentro de córrego na Baixada da Sobral — Foto: Reprodução

De acordo com Felipe, a prefeitura chegou a pavimentar a rua, porém, faltou a sinalização adequada do local.

“Agora no mês de agosto fez um ano que a prefeitura veio, asfaltou aquela região e ficou faltando fazer aquela ponte. Não fizeram a ponte e não sinalizaram também. A obra ficou daquele jeito, abandonada, e quem passa por aquela região está sujeito a passar por um pequeno transtorno. A ponte ali que não dá acesso ao outro lado”, contou.

Além da falta de sinalização, o morador explica ainda que, no período da noite, é difícil para quem transita na região enxergar o córrego de forma nítida. Conforme ele, praticamente não há iluminação no local.

“Quando vai chegando pela parte daquele buraco, fica um pouco escuro, aí quem vem de longe não consegue identificar que ele tem um relevo, que tem uma ponte. E um ponto importante também é que não está sinalizado, em nenhuma parte está sinalizando ‘obras à frente’, ‘uma ponte à frente’ ou ‘tomem cuidado’, não tem nada”, afirmou.

A ponte descrita é uma espécie de passarela, feita de madeira, que não tem corrimão ou estrutura de apoio para quem passa por ela. A estrutura foi construída para a passagem apenas de pedestres e ciclistas.

Carro passa direto por passarela e cai em córrego no Acre — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Felipe reclama ainda que a prefeitura não conversou com os moradores da região sobre a questão da sinalização da área. “Esses dias os moradores deram uma reformada nela porque estava pior [do que está no vídeo]. Mas, ela precisa de um reforço urgente e também tem uma rampa que é muito difícil para subir”, disse.

De acordo com ele, passam diariamente na região pessoas que levam os filhos à escola ou que precisam ir até um supermercado próximo.

“Então, aquela via é bastante usada pelos moradores. Já chegou a cair uma mãe com criança na bicicleta porque para a subida tem tipo uma rampinha e o acesso não é bom”, finalizou.

articles.standfirst: Keir Starmer deixou o governo britânico em julho por conta da pressão política decorrente do panorama econômico e social do país, porém ainda atuava como deputado.
articles.summary: Keir Starmer deixou o governo britânico em julho por conta da pressão política decorrente do panorama econômico e social do país, porém ainda atuava como deputado.
articles.body:
O primeiro-ministro britânico, Keir Starmer, reage ao anunciar o cronograma de sua renúncia, em frente ao número 10 da Downing Street, em Londres — Foto: REUTERS/Jaimi Joy

O ex-primeiro-ministro do Reino Unido Keir Starmer renunciou nesta terça-feira (1º) a seu assento no Parlamento britânico. Ele deixou o governo em julho.

O anúncio de Starmer veio em uma declaração enviada ao tablóide britânico "Camden New Journal", na qual ele afirmou estar "pronto para passar o bastão" e que foi "uma grande honra e privilégio" servir no Parlamento durante 11 anos.

O ex-premiê do Partido Trabalhista disse que agora focará em "assuntos internacionais", porém não deu maiores detalhes.

“Agora, vou me concentrar em outras questões, entre elas os assuntos internacionais, incluindo defesa, segurança, comércio e tecnologia, em um mundo em rápida transformação. (...) Também vou continuar, como venho fazendo há bastante tempo com outras pessoas, trabalhando no combate à violência contra mulheres e meninas. Essa é uma questão que é muito importante para mim", afirmou.

Sua renúncia provocará uma nova eleição para seu assento , que representa o município de Holborn and St. Pancras, em Londres.

Logo após deixar o governo britânico, em julho, Starmer disse à emissora britânica BBC que continuaria como parlamentar até as próximas eleições gerais no Reino Unido, que ainda não têm data marcada porém devem ocorrer até 15 de agosto de 2029.

articles.summary: Vítima de 21 anos foi socorrida após uma árvore cair sobre sua moto em São Vicente durante o vendaval que atingiu o litoral de SP nesta terça-feira.
articles.body:
Uma mulher de 21 anos ficou ferida após ser derrubada da moto em que estava durante a queda de uma árvore em São Vicente, no litoral de São Paulo. O acidente aconteceu na manhã desta terça-feira (1º), quando foram registrados ventos de até 73 km/h no município.

Câmeras de monitoramento flagraram o acidente na Avenida Angelina Pretti, na altura do bairro Jardim Irmã Dolores, por volta das 7h50.

As imagens mostram duas pessoas na motocicleta, mas há registro de apenas uma pessoa ferida. Não há informação sobre quem pilotava o veículo no momento do acidente.

Após a queda, a jovem permaneceu no chão e foi socorrida por outros dois motociclistas. De acordo com a Secretaria da Saúde (Sesau), ela apresentava dores nos membros inferiores e foi encaminhada ao pronto-socorro do Rio Branco.

Equipes da Defesa Civil fizeram a remoção da árvore e liberaram a via.

Em nota, a Sesau informou que a paciente foi acolhida e permanece em observação na unidade. A Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP) afirmou que não havia localizado registro da ocorrência até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: 'He killed her, then went back to sleep': Chilling calm of Hyderabad nurse's killer baffles cops
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: A bike mechanic accused of raping and strangling a nurse in Pahadishareef  area in Hyderabad allegedly returned to the garage where he work.
articles.body: HYDERABAD: A bike mechanic accused of raping and strangling a nurse in Pahadishareef area in Hyderabad allegedly returned to the garage where he worked and went to sleep soon after committing the crime, police said on Monday, even as investigators said he had entered the woman’s room through a window while she was asleep.The accused, a native of Bihar who came to Hyderabad in 2023 for work, was arrested for the rape and murder of the nurse.Investigators said he had allegedly been watching the woman’s movements for nearly a month before the crime.Police said the accused entered the woman’s room through a window while she was asleep. When she allegedly resisted the sexual assault, he strangled her to death.After the crime, he allegedly escaped through the same window and returned to the garage.“He was allegedly under the influence of alcohol on the day of the offence. After committing the crime, he returned to the garage and slept. He initially denied any involvement in the case,” police said.'Woman was unconscious during assault'Police said it is difficult to establish whether the woman was alive when the sexual assault took place.When asked whether the rape occurred after the murder, a police officer said, “Whether the victim had died by then or not cannot be ascertained.”However, the accused allegedly told investigators that the woman was unconscious when the assault took place.Police said the accused worked at a garage located near the window at the rear of the victim’s room.About a month before the incident, he allegedly noticed her through the window and subsequently began keeping track of her movements.Mobile data helped crack caseThe crime came to light after the nurse’s friend was unable to contact her and went to her room with a few others.Finding the door locked, they entered through the window and discovered her dead.The case was initially registered as murder. Following the medical report, police added sections relating to rape and provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.Police said the accused initially denied any role in the crime. Investigators later analysed mobile phone tower data and other evidence before questioning him further, following which he allegedly confessed.Hair strands and other forensic evidence were collected from the scene. articles.title: Kudzu was brought to America as a garden plant; scientists now warn its tangled vines can become wildfire fuel
articles.summary: US News: Kudzu arrived in the United States as an ornamental vine more than a century ago, first displayed at the Philadelphia Centennial Exposition in 1876 be.
articles.body: Kudzu arrived in the United States as an ornamental vine more than a century ago, first displayed at the Philadelphia Centennial Exposition in 1876 before being promoted for shade, livestock forage and erosion control. What began as a useful garden and agricultural plant eventually spread far beyond where it was intended, covering forests, roadsides and abandoned farmland across the South. Today, researchers are examining another consequence of its dense growth. The US Forest Service says dry kudzu litter can add substantial fuel to dormant-season fires, while vines growing into forest canopies may provide ladder fuels that allow flames to move upwards. Scientists caution that the specific effect of kudzu on wildfire behaviour remains insufficiently studied, but its ability to connect different layers of vegetation has emerged as a reason for concern.How a garden plant became wildfire fuel in AmericaKudzu, scientifically known as Pueraria montana var. lobata, is native to Asia and was introduced to the US in 1876 as an ornamental vine. USDA Forest Service records say it was used to shade porches and courtyards before becoming popular as livestock forage and later as a tool against soil erosion. During the 1930s and 1940s, federal programmes distributed millions of kudzu seedlings across the South and farmers were offered financial incentives to plant it. The plant's rapid growth eventually became a liability. It can produce vines up to about 30 centimetres a day under favourable conditions and can grow through several layers of a forest canopy before overtopping trees. By the 1950s, the government had begun withdrawing its support and kudzu was increasingly recognised as a serious weed.Scientists are looking at what happens when kudzu enters forestsThe wildfire concern begins with the way kudzu changes the structure of an invaded forest. Rather than remaining on the ground, the vine can climb shrubs and mature trees, forming dense layers of vegetation and eventually covering the canopy. A 2024 study by Ming Shen, Maofeng Tang, Wenzhe Jiao and Yingkui Li used satellite imagery to examine kudzu invasion in Knox County, Tennessee, and found that heavily invaded areas were concentrated along highways, riversides and the edges of urban forests. The researchers also found that kudzu expanded through the warmer months before rapidly losing foliage in autumn. That seasonal cycle matters because the plant can leave behind dry material as temperatures fall, potentially changing the amount and arrangement of fuel in landscapes where the vine has become established.The wildfire concern is about ladder fuelsThe key scientific concept is ladder fuel, vegetation that creates a vertical connection between fuels on the ground and those in the tree canopy. The US Forest Service explains that fuels occur in different layers, including surface, ladder and canopy fuels, and that their arrangement can influence fire behaviour and spread. Its technical guidance specifically lists vines and lianas such as kudzu as a type of ladder fuel when they create vertical continuity between lower vegetation and tree crowns. This does not mean every kudzu patch will produce a crown fire. Instead, the concern is that a dense infestation climbing from the forest floor into trees can create one of the conditions that make upward fire spread more possible.Dry kudzu can add more fuel to the forestThere is an important distinction between living kudzu and the dead material it leaves behind. Green kudzu contains substantial water and is not necessarily easy to ignite. The US Forest Service says green foliage probably does not burn well because of its high water content. The situation can change after vegetation dies back. Dense kudzu litter can provide substantial fuel for dormant-season surface fires, while dead woody vegetation beneath heavily invaded areas can add further combustible material. The agency also warns that kudzu growing into forest canopies may provide ladder fuels that increase the potential for crown fires. However, the Forest Service describes these effects as scenarios that were still speculative in its assessment and says additional research is needed to establish how kudzu changes the fire ecology of invaded forests.New fire research shows why vertical fuel is importantRecent research into ladder fuels strengthens the scientific basis for understanding this mechanism, even though it was not conducted specifically on kudzu. A 2026 study published in Fire Ecology examined ladder-fuel ignition through 92 controlled experiments involving live manzanita and incense cedar foliage and branches positioned above a surface fire. Researchers including Yucheng He and US Forest Service scientist David R. Weise found that ignition probability was influenced by factors including temperature, fuel characteristics and the height of the ladder fuel above the surface fire. The study showed why vertical fuel continuity matters in wildfire behaviour. It cannot be used to claim that kudzu itself was proven to ignite forest canopies, but it provides experimental evidence for the broader fire mechanism that makes climbing vines such as kudzu a concern.Kudzu can survive fire and return quicklyFire also does not necessarily solve the kudzu problem. The US Forest Service says the plant can survive fire through its underground root crowns and can resprout after burning. In some documented cases, kudzu returned to its previous level of dominance by the second growing season after a dormant-season fire. The agency also notes that dry kudzu litter can contribute to dormant-season surface fires and that heat from fire may potentially encourage germination by breaking seed dormancy, although the importance of this process in natural landscapes remains uncertain. This creates a difficult management problem because burning an infestation may remove vegetation above ground without eliminating the established root system that allows kudzu to return.A 600-acre wildfire exposed the concernThe issue gained a real-world dimension in western North Carolina in March 2025, when a power line brought down by strong winds sparked a wildfire near Tryon. The blaze ultimately burned more than 600 acres, according to reporting cited by Inside Climate News. The incident is important to the kudzu story, but the distinction over cause matters. Kudzu did not ignite the fire and should not be described as the cause. The ignition came from the power line. The concern was what happened after ignition in a landscape where kudzu had formed extensive vegetation. Fire behaviour depends on fuel quantity, moisture, arrangement and connectivity, making dense climbing vegetation relevant to the way a fire can move through a forest.Scientists are not saying kudzu causes wildfiresThe evidence does not support a simple claim that kudzu causes wildfires. Instead, the concern is that large infestations can alter the fuel structure of a forest. Chelsea Nagy of the University of Colorado Boulder, quoted by Inside Climate News, explained that fuel amount, structure, connectivity and moisture all influence fire risk. That principle is consistent with the broader US Forest Service description of wildfire fuels. Kudzu becomes particularly interesting because it can occupy the ground layer while climbing into shrubs and trees, potentially connecting fuel layers that would otherwise be more separated. The US Forest Service, however, has explicitly said that the specific effects of kudzu on fire regimes require further research. That uncertainty should remain part of any assessment of the plant's wildfire threat.Volunteers are removing the vine from forestsWhile scientists continue to examine the fire implications, conservation groups are already tackling kudzu on the ground. At Norman Wilder Forest near Tryon, North Carolina, the Kudzu Warriors, a volunteer group organised through Conserving Carolina, have been removing the invasive vine since 2011. Volunteers follow vines back to their root crowns and dig them out, because cutting the visible growth alone can allow the plant to regenerate. Conserving Carolina says large parts of the 185-acre preserve that were once covered by kudzu are now free of the vine, with native wildflowers and other vegetation returning. The organisation continues to hold Kudzu Warriors workdays at the forest, showing that the restoration effort remains active rather than being a one-time project.Removing kudzu restores more than the forest floorThe restoration work offers a wider ecological benefit than simply removing a potentially hazardous fuel. Conserving Carolina reports that areas once covered by solid mats of kudzu at Norman Wilder Forest now support native vegetation, while restoration projects have included planting native prairie plants and grasses in areas cleared of the vine. Removing kudzu allows sunlight and growing space to return to plants that had been suppressed by the invasive species. It can also remove dense mats of vegetation and dead material from the landscape. While there is not enough evidence to claim that every kudzu removal project will measurably reduce wildfire risk, reducing an invasive vine's dominance can simultaneously address habitat degradation and one potential source of connected fuel.The fight is difficult because kudzu keeps coming backKudzu is notoriously difficult to eradicate once it becomes established. Its large underground root system stores energy that allows the plant to recover after cutting, grazing or fire. The US Forest Service says complete eradication requires killing all major and minor root crowns and notes that well-established stands can require many years of treatment. Conserving Carolina's experience shows why repeated work is necessary. Its Kudzu Warriors have spent years removing the vine from Norman Wilder Forest, and the organisation continues to describe the fight as ongoing even after substantial areas have been restored. That long-term approach is important because preventing a dense infestation from returning may be more realistic than expecting a single treatment to eliminate the plant permanently.An old garden plant has become a modern fire-management concernKudzu's journey from ornamental vine to invasive species shows how dramatically the consequences of introducing a plant can change over time. It was first welcomed in the US for its attractive growth and shade, later promoted as forage and erosion control, and eventually recognised as an invasive plant capable of overwhelming native vegetation. Now, its dense growth is drawing attention from fire scientists and land managers because dry litter can add fuel and vines extending into tree canopies can potentially create ladder-fuel connections. The evidence does not show that kudzu independently causes wildfires, and researchers still need more direct studies of kudzu's effects on fire behaviour. But the mechanism is scientifically plausible, the US Forest Service explicitly identifies kudzu as a potential ladder fuel, and recent experiments demonstrate why vertical fuel connections matter. That makes controlling dense kudzu infestations relevant not only to ecological restoration but also to the broader challenge of managing wildfire fuels.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: At least five killed as ammunition-laden vehicle explodes in Syria’s Idlib
articles.summary: Several also injured in incident that took place in Idlib countryside, state media reports.
articles.body:
A vehicle loaded with ammunition has exploded in the town of Binnish in the Idlib countryside in northwestern Syria, according to Syrian authorities and a security source quoted by Syria’s official news agency, SANA.

At least five people were killed and five others wounded in the explosion on Tuesday, according to Syrian broadcaster Al-Ikhbariya. Authorities have not released reports regarding the cause of the blast.

Earlier, the Idlib Emergency and Disaster Management Directorate had reported that two people had been killed, and at least eight others wounded. Two vehicles in the vicinity were also destroyed.

Emergency response teams were dispatched to the scene, and the wounded were transported to nearby hospitals.

The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said the explosion had caused panic among residents.

The rights group reported that ammunition had continued exploding after the initial incident, creating the risk of further blasts as well as flying ammunition and shrapnel.

The AFP news agency, referring to an unnamed government official, reported that the vehicle belonged to a local arms dealer in the town of Binnish.

The Idlib region was a hub for rebel armed groups before the overthrow of longtime former ruler Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, and explosions are not uncommon at military sites and arms depots, with authorities often not announcing the cause.

An explosion in November at a warehouse containing missiles and ammunition in the town of Kafr Takharim killed five people and wounded nine others, according to the military.

Three months earlier, an explosion at a war remnants depot on the outskirts of Idlib city killed four people, authorities said.

articles.title: Ikea cuts prices as customers struggle with rising cost of living
articles.summary: The Swedish retailer has seen revenue decline as the rising cost of living reduces people's ability to buy new furniture.
articles.body:
Swedish furniture giant Ikea is cutting prices across hundreds of products in Europe to woo customers struggling with deepening cost-of-living pressures.

Ikea has seen revenue decline over the past two years as the rising cost of living reduces people's ability to invest in new furniture and home renovations.

The company is spending €1.2bn (£1bn) on the price cuts to items including the Billy bookcase and Kallax storage units, with reductions of up to 28% on certain products.

Ikea said it could make the cuts by making savings throughout the supply chain, such as packaging costs, but acknowledged profits may take a hit.

Ingka, the franchisee which operates most of Ikea's European stores, said the cuts were "not an activity or short-term campaign".

"It's about making IKEA more affordable when people need it most, even if it means accepting a lower margin," said Juvencio Maeztu, chief executive of Ingka. "The cost of living is increasing and it's getting tougher and tougher for many people."

He added: "For many people, home is a bedroom in a shared house, and it's even more important to offer storage and organised solutions."

Ikea has reduced its prices several times in recent years, even as it caused a hit to the company's revenue and profit in its most recent earnings report.

The latest specific reductions vary slightly by country. Price cuts for British customers include the Kallax shelving unit going from £60 to £49 and the Billy bookcase being cut by £10 to £25.

Ikea is also trying to attract new customers by opening smaller stores in central areas, such as London's Oxford Street and Churchill Square in Brighton.

In 2024 it launched its own second-hand online marketplace in a bid to rival sites like eBay and Facebook Marketplace.

Despite a recent uptick, consumer confidence in Europe is at its lowest level for almost three years due to concerns about inflation and the cost of living, according to EU figures.

British consumers, meanwhile, are becoming more optimistic about the economy and their own finances, following a truce in the Middle East, but analysts have warned that inflation and the rising cost of living could dent consumer confidence in the coming months.

Ikea operates over 500 stores worldwide under a franchise system.

Many of its minimalist, self-assembled products have become ubiquitous in homes across Europe.

But it has faced criticism from environmentalists for contributing to a culture of disposable furniture and excess packaging.

articles.title: A four-month-old baby was buried without a marker in 1906; 120 years later her cemetery finally gave her a headstone
articles.summary: US News: In 1906, a 4-month-old baby named ‘Maytie Raker’ became the first person to be buried at Inglewood Park Cemetery in California. Her death came at the .
articles.body: In 1906, a 4-month-old baby named ‘Maytie Raker’ became the first person to be buried at Inglewood Park Cemetery in California. Her death came at the beginning of the cemetery's long history, yet for the next 120 years, there was no marker to identify where she lay. Generations passed without a permanent tribute to the infant, whose short life had almost disappeared from public view. A review of historical records eventually brought her story back into the light, prompting cemetery and city leaders to honour her with a headstone. According to CBS, the new marker was installed to correct a long-overlooked part of the cemetery's history. The ceremony did more than identify a grave. It also restored Maytie's place in the story of a community and ensured that the baby who had been forgotten for more than a century would finally be remembered.Story of four-month-old Maytie Raker who didn’t get the marker at her graveMaytie Raker was only four months old when she died in 1906. According to CBS, she was the first child of King D. and Jessie Raker and became the first person laid to rest at Inglewood Park Cemetery on 20 July 1906. Despite holding such an important place in the cemetery's history, her grave remained unmarked. A review of historical records later revealed that no permanent marker had been placed at the site for generations. The story also carries a deeper sadness because Maytie was not the only young child in the family to die. Her younger sister, Hattie, also died in infancy the following year. Their brother, Alexander, however, lived until 1993, carrying the Raker family line forward. For decades, Maytie's story remained largely absent from the visible landscape of the cemetery. While her grave existed, there was nothing above it to tell visitors her name or explain why she held such a unique place in its history.Recognising the forgotten grave of the four-month-old infant girlMore than a century after Maytie's burial, historical records helped bring attention to her unmarked grave. According to CBS, cemetery leadership commissioned a permanent marker to ensure that her place in the cemetery's history would finally be recognised. The decision was supported by city and park leaders, who gathered to honour the child and acknowledge the long delay in marking her burial site. Inglewood City Councilmember Alex Padilla described the occasion as an opportunity to do justice to the Raker family. PEOPLE also reported that the effort was intended to correct history and celebrate Maytie's memory. The child had been buried at the very beginning of Inglewood Park Cemetery's existence, making her story closely connected to the history of the institution itself. The new headstone therefore became more than a memorial to one child. It was also an acknowledgement that even the earliest chapters of a community's history deserve to be remembered.What does Maytie's new headstone look likeCBS reported that the headstone is decorated with butterflies and a flower, while the words ‘Forever in our hearts’ appear alongside Maytie Raker's name. Maytie is buried next to her sister Hattie, whose grave marker carries similar imagery. Hattie's stone includes the words ‘Resting in Heaven's Garden,’ creating a visual connection between the two sisters who both died in infancy. PEOPLE reported that placing Maytie's marker beside her sister's headstone gave the site an added sense of family remembrance. For more than a century, visitors could have passed the burial site without knowing who rested there. The new marker changes that, making her name and story part of the cemetery's visible history.Importance of ceremony to the communityInglewood Park Cemetery has a particularly long connection to the surrounding community. According to PEOPLE, Brendt Stallings, the cemetery's chief executive, said the institution had existed even before Inglewood officially became a city. That history made Maytie's story especially meaningful. She was not simply another person buried there; she was the first. Her unmarked grave represented a missing piece of the cemetery's own story. Inglewood Mayor James T. Butts stressed on the lasting role of the cemetery, noting that while other major structures may eventually wear out, the cemetery will continue to preserve the memories of those buried there.What does Maytie's story say about remembranceMaytie Raker lived for only four months, yet her story has endured for 120 years because historical records eventually revealed what had been overlooked. According to PEOPLE, the ceremony was described as a ‘gone, but never forgotten’ moment. That sentiment now has a permanent physical form in the cemetery. Maytie's new headstone is a small memorial to a life that ended more than a century ago. But it also serves as a reminder that history is not always preserved perfectly. Sometimes, names disappear from public view, records are overlooked, and graves remain anonymous. For Maytie Raker, however, that anonymity has finally ended. articles.title: UK long-term borrowing costs highest since 1998 ahead of October Budget
articles.summary: Higher borrowing costs have piled fresh pressure on Andy Burnham ahead of his first Budget.
articles.body:
Long-term government borrowing costs have risen to a 28-year high, putting further pressure on Prime Minister Andy Burnham ahead of his first Budget next month.

The yield on a 30-year gilt — a loan to the British government — rose to 5.89% on Tuesday, the highest since 1998.

Borrowing costs in the US, Japan and Europe have hit similar highs in recent days, reflecting investors' concerns about inflation, state borrowing levels and spending levels by large tech companies on AI.

Burnham told the House of Commons his government's "bedrock", as it seeks to tackle the cost-of-living crisis, will be "fiscal responsibility".

All of those factors will make the Budget process trickier for Burnham, who on Tuesday addressed MPs for the first time as prime minister , and his Chancellor John Healey.

Burnham told the House of Commons the economy and the cost of living were "the biggest issues facing the country".

Higher borrowing costs will reduce the amount of headroom the government has against its self-imposed fiscal rules, limiting the amount Healey can spend on consumer-friendly measures to ease the cost of living.

Despite the squeezed public finances, Burnham said said he would bring about "more substantial change" to ease living costs.

"Britain is not where any of us would wish it to be," he added.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused Burnham of "living in the past".

"His diagnosis is completely wrong," she told the House of Commons. "His theory of growth is completely wrong. He thinks that if Government spends more money, we will all get richer.

The chancellor has previously said he will stick to a set of fiscal rules imposed by his predecessor Rachel Reeves that restrict borrowing. These rules are designed to help markets have clarity about the path of borrowing.

The more that is forecast to be spent on interest payments, the more likely that there will be a squeeze on spending or some form of tax rise to meet these rules.

On top of that, higher government rates can feed through to higher business and household borrowing costs, and so weigh on the economy.

Burnham was already facing a tough balancing act with taxing and spending, due to pressures on defence and the cost of living.

As well as the rise to 30-year gilt yields, the yield on the benchmark 10-year gilt rose to 5.22% on Tuesday. This is its highest rate since June 2008, at the height of the global financial crisis.

Gilt yields move counter to the value of the bonds, meaning their prices fall when yields rise.

Around the world there are warning lights flashing from the markets for government debt.

Global markets reacted in particular after suggestions in the US that its central bank could raise rates. Japan is also facing pressure to raise rates.

The Chancellor is in the USA attending a meeting of global finance ministers and central bankers. He told the G20 that the UK had the fastest growth in the G7 in 2026 so far, that productivity was improving and that the UK was cutting its borrowing at the fastest rate of the major economies.

US borrowing costs hit a fresh high on Tuesday as renewed strikes in the Middle East pushed up oil prices and heightened concerns over inflation.

Karen Ward, JP Morgan's chief market strategist for Europe, said governments around the world want to increase spending and are turning to borrowing to fund it.

And she told the BBC's World at One they are increasingly having to compete with major technology companies raising money to invest in the AI revolution, pushing up the amount of interest being charged.

"Markets are getting a lot more choice about who they are going to lend to and at what interest rates," she added.

Burnham has rolled out a series of interventions to support consumers and businesses since entering Downing Street, and is expected to prioritise further measures to ease the cost of living in the Budget on 28 October.

Ward urged Burnham and Healey to set out how they will fund any fresh spending on defence and the cost of living, and how those lending the government money will be paid back.

Kathleen Brooks, research director at investment company XTB, told the BBC News Channel: "Of course, this is red lights flashing."

"We are used to pockets of volatility, it has been volatile few months," she says.

But record levels of government debt and a record tax take mean "these are not comfortable times for the new government and the new chancellor," she says.

Every time bond yields rise, the UK has to pay more on the debt interest, she says.

articles.title: DRC: Ebola fears grow as children return to school
articles.summary: Parents fear school could fuel Ebola spread as authorities shift high-risk pupils to home learning.
articles.body:
Goma, DR Congo – Children across the Democratic Republic of the Congo are returning to school on Tuesday as the country battles its largest Ebola outbreak on record, prompting concern among parents and teachers in the worst-hit province of Ituri.

Government figures showed 6,041 confirmed cases and 2,911 deaths as of August 31, surpassing the previous worst outbreak, which ran from 2018 to 2020.

Six of the country’s 26 provinces are affected. Ituri, in the northeast, remains the epicentre, with 4,802 confirmed cases recorded as of August 26.

In Bunia, Ituri’s provincial capital, parents are questioning whether schools should reopen while the outbreak continues to spread.

“As a parent, I am concerned about the announcement that schools are reopening, especially as we are facing the Ebola outbreak in our region. We are asking the government what measures they will put in place to protect children from this disease,” said Dieudonne Lotsima, a father of three and resident of Bunia.

Lotsima believes classes should be postponed until a vaccine specifically effective against the virus causing the outbreak becomes available.

“Children are children,” he told Al Jazeera. “They may not wash their hands at the washbasins, and if they become infected, they risk infecting the whole family. This return to school is uncertain, and if we do not take steps to protect the children, I do not know what we can do.”

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a species of ebolavirus different from the Zaire ebolavirus, which has caused most previous Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

There is currently no approved vaccine or treatment specifically for Bundibugyo virus disease. Ervebo, the vaccine approved against Zaire ebolavirus, is being given to front-line health workers, but its effectiveness against Bundibugyo has not been established. The World Health Organization is supporting a clinical trial to assess whether it can protect against the strain responsible for the current outbreak.

How is the government reopening schools?

Rather than impose a nationwide closure, the government is using different arrangements according to the level of Ebola risk.

In the highest-risk areas, pupils will study from home using printed materials and radio programmes, according to the Ministry of Education. Workbooks and learning sheets covering essential parts of the curriculum will be distributed, while local and community radio stations will broadcast programmes to accompany them. Families without radios may also be provided with them.

Raissa Malu, the minister of education, said on August 18 that 40 of the country’s 138 educational subdivisions in Ebola-affected provinces were affected by the outbreak. Eighteen were classified as high risk.

The government has divided areas into three categories: green, where there is no reported Ebola transmission; orange, where areas are affected but can continue with additional precautions; and red, where the risk is considered highest.

“We are, in fact, going to introduce a system of worksheets that will be produced in line with the curriculum, focusing on essential knowledge, and distributed to children to enable them to continue their work at home,” Malu told Al Jazeera.

She stressed that the arrangement was not online or internet-based teaching.

But Catherine Neema, a mother of two in Bunia, remains unconvinced.

“I’m not sure I’ll send my child to school. When the children start school, there will be too many people. People may come into close contact with one another and become infected,” she said.

Neema said her eldest child began the holidays when confirmed Ebola cases stood at about 1,500, with 470 deaths.

The Ituri 1 Teachers’ Inter-Union Committee says the epidemiological situation is not conducive to a safe return to school.

Budju Lobo Isaac, a trade union member, said schools needed basic health measures before children and teachers returned.

“We cannot sacrifice the lives of children and teachers just to stick to a timetable. Before reopening schools, we must ensure minimum health and safety standards are in place: handwashing facilities, hand sanitiser, thermal scanners, and monitoring and support for teachers,” he told Al Jazeera.

Education officials have also been training staff in Ituri to identify risky behaviour, promote preventive measures, and educate pupils about Ebola.

“We have trained inspectors, senior officials from the provincial directorate, and other members of teachers’ unions,” said Jean-Baptiste Ngona Kivi, acting head of the General Education Service in the Ituri 1 educational province. “They will be deployed to the sub-districts to pass on this training on Ebola protection techniques to headteachers and teachers.”

Professor Yap Boum, incident manager at the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention for the response to the Bundibugyo outbreak, sees the return to school as an opportunity to reach families with information about Ebola.

“Once they have been made aware of the Ebola virus disease, when they return home, they also help to raise awareness amongst adults,” he told Al Jazeera. “So this is another opportunity we see in children returning to school.”

articles.title: Kyla's Do You Mind named TikTok's UK song of the summer
articles.summary: Kyla's 2008 track Do You Mind gained worldwide recognition in 2016 when rapper Drake sampled it on One Dance.
articles.body:
British singer Kyla's Do You Mind has been named as TikTok's song of the summer in the UK after the noughties garage track experienced a resurgence on the app.

The song gained popularity when it was first released in 2008, but it became known worldwide in 2016 when Canadian rapper Drake sampled it on his chart-topping single One Dance.

It has now found a new audience by trending on TikTok, generating more than 500 million views from about 650,000 videos posted in the UK over the summer, according to the platform.

Kyla, who created the song with her husband DJ Paleface, tells BBC Newsbeat it is "surreal" but "incredible" that Do You Mind is getting another moment nearly 20 years on.

"Back in 2016, even though it had all that success, it still felt like: 'Oh, it's because you're with Drake'," she says.

"I think this time around it was like: 'Well this is actually me'."

Singer Jorja Smith brought Kyla out on stage during her headline slot at All Points East festival in London last month to perform the track together.

Kyla says hearing about 40,000 people sing the song back to her was an "incredible" experience which made her want to cry.

"It feels nice because it's mine. I'm happy," she says.

The song has soundtracked a range of TikTok videos, from lip-syncs to outfit reveals.

But Kyla says she personally loves the ones which play on the lyrics "baby" and "honey" by using dolls and real honey as props.

UK garage music is experiencing a resurgence, with artists like Sammy Virji, AJ Tracey and Disclosure incorporating the sound into their work, while noughties girl group Mis-Teeq are reuniting .

As part of the garage movement, Manchester-based artist Silva Bumpa's On 2nite has taken third place in the latest TikTok chart, and Prospa and Cloonee's Free Your Mind has made it to number seven.

"I feel like a lot of people are saying funky house is back, then I'm hearing garage is back, but I do think it's a collection of people's tunes that they've really loved over time and they're just enjoying them again," Kyla says about the revival.

"The younger generation are just learning these songs but they've been there for time."

Do You Mind is not the only older song the platform has introduced to new audiences through trends this summer.

Oasis' 1995 classic Wonderwall has secured the title of second biggest UK song of the summer on TikTok after becoming the unofficial soundtrack to England's World Cup journey.

Its popularity in mass singalongs for fans prompted a 6,800% surge in searches for it since the start of the tournament, according to Tiktok.

The track also featured in more than 300,000 videos and climbed back up the singles chart to number two.

The continued love for the Britpop band also helped their track Champagne Supernova make it to number six in the TikTok top 10 list.

The trend for nostalgic tracks appears to have been worldwide as US singer Katy Perry's The One That Got Away has been crowned TikTok's global song of the summer nearly 15 years after it was first released in 2011.

It has featured in more than 15 million TikTok videos, with Perry saying it is "surreal" to see the track "having this moment all these years later".

"From seeing it being chosen in the 'choose your own adventure' section of my Lifetimes Tour concert film to seeing people discover it on TikTok and make it part of their own stories has been really special to watch," she says.

"It's nice to revisit an amazing chapter while watching another unfold."

articles.title: What to know about the US primary election in Massachusetts
articles.summary: Competitive House races and a Senate showdown will put US Democrats’ progressive-moderate divide to the test.
articles.body:
Voters in the US state of Massachusetts head to the polls on Tuesday for a primary election featuring a closely watched United States Senate contest between Democratic incumbent Senator Ed Markey and US Representative Seth Moulton.

The race is the latest contest that pits the Democratic Party’s progressive and moderate wings against each other. But in a twist, Moulton, the challenger, is part of the moderate New Democrat Coalition, while Markey, the longtime progressive incumbent, is fighting to hold on to his seat.

Voters will also decide competitive Democratic primaries in the 6th and 8th Congressional Districts, as well as races for the state’s governor, state legislature, and district attorney.

What time do polls open and close in Massachusetts?

The Massachusetts primary is Tuesday, September 1, 2026. Polls open at 7am ET (11:00 GMT) and close at 8pm ET (midnight GMT).

What are the key races in the Massachusetts primary?

In the 6th District, voters will choose a Democratic nominee to succeed Moulton. The top contenders include former local election official Dan Koh, financial technology executive John Beccia, and Massachusetts State Representative Tram Nguyen.

Koh enters Tuesday as the leading fundraiser, with about $4.7m in contributions, and has endorsements from former US President Joe Biden and former Vice President Kamala Harris. Nguyen has raised about $895,000, while Beccia has boosted his campaign’s spending power with a $4m personal loan.

The winner will face Republican Micah Jones, who is unopposed for his party’s nomination.

In the 8th District, 13-term Democratic incumbent Representative Stephen Lynch, 71, faces a primary challenge from progressive attorney Patrick Roath, 39, who is endorsed by Leaders We Deserve, the political action committee (PAC) headed by gun-safety activist and political organiser David Hogg.

Roath has criticised the centrist voting record of Lynch, who broke with Democrats to vote against former US President Barack Obama’s Affordable Care Act in March 2010, and who was Massachusetts’s only congressional member to vote for current US President Donald Trump’s Laken Riley Act, which requires federal law enforcement to detain and deport immigrants who have been charged with nonviolent crimes regardless of whether those charges ever result in a conviction.

The winner will face a midterm election against Republican Robert Burke, who runs uncontested and who lost his 2024 bid for Congress to Lynch.

In the gubernatorial race, the Democratic primary is effectively uncontested, with incumbent Governor Maura Healey running for the Democratic nomination, but with two Republican candidates vying for Healey’s seat. Brian Shortsleeve and Michael Roger Minogue, who are running in the GOP primary, are both military veterans with business backgrounds. The most notable difference between the two candidates is that Shortsleeve backs abortion rights, while Minogue does not. Both of them have supported Trump.

Who is running in the Massachusetts US Senate primary?

The biggest statewide contest is the Democratic US Senate primary between Markey and Moulton.

Markey is seeking a third full term, but faces a primary challenge from Moulton.

Markey, who turned 80 in July, entered the US Senate in 2013 after nearly 37 years in the US House of Representatives. He last faced a competitive primary in 2020, when he defeated then-Representative Joseph Kennedy III by 10 points. Moulton, a six-term congressman and Marine Corps veteran, briefly sought the Democratic presidential nomination in 2020.

Age has been a central theme of Moulton’s campaign. Markey, who turned 80 in July, is the oldest Senate Democrat running for re-election this year. Moulton, 47, has called for “generational change” in the Democratic Party, and argues that Markey is too old to represent a generation confronting challenges like artificial intelligence (AI).

Markey came under pressure during a recent debate, when he was asked whether he uses AI platforms such as ChatGPT or Claude in his work. Markey responded that he uses whatever is available through his iPhone or iPad, saying he did not know which companies his devices might be using.

Moulton seized on the exchange, arguing that leaders need to understand the technologies they will be responsible for regulating.

“Senator, if you don’t even know what you’re using on your phone or your iPad, this is why we need a new generation of leaders to regulate these technologies,” Moulton said, calling Markey’s loose grasp of technology “potentially disqualifying”.

Markey defended his record on technology, arguing that familiarity with individual AI products is less important than establishing safeguards around the technology. He has pointed to legislation addressing AI’s effects on children, workers, civil rights and the environment.

Markey has won the endorsement of the High School Democrats of America and the College Democrats of America, as well as support from prominent progressives including US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York and Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont. Markey also has the support of US Senator Elizabeth Warren, a fellow Democrat from Massachusetts.

“Ed Markey is one of the strongest progressive voices in the United States Senate,” Sanders said in his endorsement of Markey. “He has been an ally in taking on the billionaires, Big Tech, Wall Street and private equity as they continue to try to take over every aspect of our lives and further corrupt our government.”

Recent polling has shown Markey with a sizable lead over Moulton.

A University of Massachusetts Amherst/WCVB poll conducted August 5-12 found Markey leading Moulton 60 percent to 32 percent, with 7 percent undecided.
